correctness.rationale: PASS: For the finite irreducible birth–death chain, G(k)=Na-(a+b)k and the exact quadratic generator yield E[X]=Nr and V=Nr(1-r)(A+Nh)/(A+h), r=a/A, A=a+b. Positive-lag covariance is V exp(-At). Independent freshly redrawn binomial thinning gives m=pNr, v=p²V+m(1-p), c_j=p²V exp(-j A Δ). Thus q=c2/c1, s=c1²/c2=p²V, p=1-(v-s)/m and A=-log(q)/Δ. For each integer N, r_N=m/(Np), R_N=s/(pm-m²/N), h=A(R_N-1)/(N-R_N). Necessary and sufficient positive-rate inequalities 1<R_N<N reduce algebraically to strict L<N<U, L=(s+m²)/(pm), U=m²/(pm-s) only when pm>s. This proves the complete interval including N≥2, boundary exclusion, singleton/unbounded regimes and redundant further positive lags; no finite-data inference claim. Independently reconstructed detailed-balance stationary laws, exact moments and size inequalities for 6 parameter choices (N=2,3,4,6,7), including singleton N=4 example.

originality.rationale: PASS, best of knowledge: earlier Kirman/noisy-voter work gives latent finite-state distributions and relaxation, but not the inverse fiber of unknown N and p from precisely m,v,c1,c2. The published two-visit closed N-mixture theorem identifies p and full abundance distribution for a fixed latent count between visits; it does not imply this moving birth–death, unequal-lag exponential-covariance inverse set, nor the finite-vs-unbounded N phase. The reused binomial thinning formula alone is not the novel assertion. Earlier detection-identifiability or latent Markov inference could overlap; full Kirman 1993 paper not inspected.
